one_line_purpose: Real-time audio quality assessment for voice apps.
problem_solved: Assesses if an audio recording is clean enough to process for voice applications.

tech_stack.storage: Local file system for audio files and calibration data.
tech_stack.deployment: Python package (installable via pip), command-line interface, local execution.

architecture_summary: The system is a Python library that processes audio, primarily using Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques. It calculates frame-level acoustic metrics (e.g., HNR, Energy SNR, spectral flatness, RMS, noise floor, spectral concentration, clipping ratio) which are then aggregated over a rolling window. A central assessment logic combines these metrics to assign a quality tier ('excellent', 'good', 'fair', 'poor'). For real-time streaming, a LiveDetector employs a hysteresis buffer to stabilize tier changes. It includes an optional neural backend (DNSMOS) for reference scoring.
key_features: Real-time and file-based audio quality assessment.
Categorizes audio quality into 'excellent', 'good', 'fair', or 'poor' tiers.
Provides detailed acoustic metrics including Harmonic-to-Noise Ratio (HNR), Energy SNR, Background dBA, Spectral Flatness, and Temporal Variance.
Utilizes `max(HNR, energy SNR)` to estimate mixing SNR, suitable for both speech and sustained singing.
DSP-focused core library (NumPy/SciPy), CPU-only by default.
Features a `LiveDetector` with hysteresis for stable real-time streaming analysis.
Includes a command-line interface for file assessment and live microphone monitoring.
Offers an optional neural backend integration for Microsoft DNSMOS (P.835) reference scoring.
notable_code_decisions: Prioritizing `max(HNR, energy SNR)` for mixing SNR estimation to robustly handle both speech and singing audio.
Implementation of a hysteresis buffer in `LiveDetector` to prevent quality tier flickering in real-time streaming.
Extensive use of NumPy and SciPy for efficient, CPU-only Digital Signal Processing (DSP) in the core library.
Development of a microphone auto-calibration mechanism to adapt to varying hardware and OS audio processing.
Shifting from a spectral peak-vs-floor SNR approach (v0.1.x) to `max(HNR, energy SNR)` as the primary tier driver.
Defining explicit SNR and HNR thresholds for quality tier assignments, tuned based on benchmark results.
Deterministic test set generation for benchmarking through fixed random seeds.
tradeoffs_and_limitations: Requires one-time microphone calibration for each new machine or mic setup.
Background dBA measurement is a proxy, not a certified acoustic dB meter using IEC 61672 A-weighted filters.
Does not include built-in echo cancellation or noise suppression, assuming reasonable audio input.
Detection accuracy may vary if the operating system pre-processes microphone audio.
The optional DNSMOS neural backend introduces significant latency (880 ms median) compared to the DSP path (15 ms).
Performance on 'clean_vocal' benchmark category shows lower exact tier accuracy (30.0%) in v0.3.0 compared to previous versions.
Calibrated specifically for 'recording quality' (clean enough to process) rather than subjective human sound preference.
what_it_demonstrates: Application of Digital Signal Processing (DSP) techniques (e.g., FFT, autocorrelation, RMS, various SNR calculations) for feature extraction from audio.
Construction of a real-time audio processing pipeline in Python, capable of continuous analysis from live streams.
Development of a multi-metric classification system to assign qualitative tiers to audio recordings.
Implementation of a robust streaming detector incorporating hysteresis for stable, flicker-free real-time quality assessments.
Strategies for benchmarking and validating audio quality assessment algorithms against established datasets and ground truth metrics.
Creation of a user-friendly command-line interface for interacting with audio analysis tools.
Methods for local device calibration to account for hardware and environmental variations in audio input.
